correction: Keep the creator's exact 11-slide copy and replace the rejected single-incident visual route with a lived day-in-the-life relationship montage built from instantly readable social and domestic scenes.

exact_copy.text:
We’re not married yet.
But try telling that to our habits.

Every plan starts with:
“Ek minute, usse poochna padega.”

Every small decision becomes
a two-person meeting.

Then five minutes later:
“Ghar pahunch ke text karna.”

Shaadi abhi baaki hai.
Par “hum” toh kab ke ban chuke hain.

story_arc_lock: unofficial -> shared decisions -> shared stress -> real friction -> care surviving friction -> no vows yet -> already an us

visual_story_correction.creator_diagnosis: The prior broken-key continuity route was too engineered and made the copy serve a prop story. The creator wants large, recognisable relationship situations that a viewer understands immediately.
visual_story_correction.visual_grammar: A warm day-in-the-life relationship sitcom: distinct office, dining-table, living-room, doorway, and separate-home scenes connected by one emotional arc rather than one symbolic object.
visual_story_correction.governing_rule: Every frame must stage the exact relationship behaviour named by the copy through obvious action, reaction, blocking, and consequence. No private metaphor may be required.

slides.scene: Morning outside an office lobby or cafe. Aachu casually straightens Zuv's office ID lanyard while he hands her the coffee he has already ordered for her. Both actions happen automatically while they continue moving, proving a practiced habit without wedding or cohabitation imagery.
slides.camera: Medium-wide three-quarter two-shot with both faces and both reciprocal actions readable.
slides.silent_read: They already know and complete each other's routines.

slides.scene: Inside Zuv's office, two friends or colleagues sit and stand directly in front of him while proposing a plan. They wait mid-conversation as Zuv gives them a natural one-minute palm, turns slightly aside, and lifts his phone to his ear to call Aachu.
slides.camera: Over-the-friends medium shot that makes their waiting reactions and Zuv's phone gesture equally legible.
slides.silent_read: Before agreeing to the plan, his first instinct is to check with her.

slides.scene: That evening, Aachu and Zuv sit opposite each other at a dining table turned into an absurdly serious meeting: papers, two notebooks, an open laptop, pens, a calendar, and two mugs surround two tiny curtain-fabric swatches at the centre. Both lean in, point at the swatches, and take the small choice completely seriously.
slides.camera: High three-quarter or overhead-wide view so the two-person meeting geometry and comic paperwork are unmistakable.
slides.silent_read: A tiny choice has become a formal joint conference.

slides.scene: Later in the same home, one partner alone receives the problem: Zuv sits forward with one troubling work document or laptop at the coffee table, hand pressed to his forehead. Aachu has just entered the edge of the room and notices his face; she is not yet solving it.
slides.camera: Tight single-person-biased medium shot with Zuv and the single problem dominant; Aachu only as the noticing reaction at the edge.
slides.silent_read: The problem belongs to one person.

slides.scene: The same problem now sits between them on the coffee table. Aachu and Zuv occupy opposite sides of the sofa in matching thinking postures, both staring at the same page or laptop, each independently carrying the full worry.
slides.camera: Symmetrical wide frontal shot with the single problem centred and their mirrored stress readable at once.
slides.silent_read: One person's worry has entered both heads.

slides.scene: The shared stress tips into a full cushion fight. From opposite sides of the living room, Aachu and Zuv throw sofa cushions toward each other; one cushion is frozen mid-air and each still grips another. Both have tight brows, tense shoulders, planted feet, and open mouths mid-argument with no smile or playful bounce. Papers on the coffee table have shifted, but neither person is humiliated or physically threatened.
slides.camera: Low wide action angle followed by opposing movement, with both whole bodies, owned hands, and the airborne cushion clearly separated.
slides.silent_read: They fight properly and equally, not as a cute posed disagreement.

slides.scene: Five minutes later in the same messy living room, cushions remain scattered. Zuv is at the open front door putting on his shoes or lifting his bag to leave. Aachu remains near the sofa, still stiff and annoyed, looking away while calling after him. He pauses at the threshold to hear her but does not walk back.
slides.camera: Wide inside-looking-out view that keeps the fight residue, Aachu, Zuv, and his outward movement in one frame.
slides.silent_read: The anger remains, but she still tells him to get home safely.

slides.scene: From the corridor behind Zuv, he continues walking away with tight shoulders and an unsmiling three-quarter profile. Through the open doorway behind him, Aachu sharply picks up one fallen cushion and turns away. Neither approaches the other.
slides.camera: Long corridor wide shot with Zuv foreground moving outward and Aachu smaller but readable inside the doorway.
slides.silent_read: They are still angry; the earlier care did not erase the fight.

slides.scene: Later, Aachu sits alone on the same sofa with the room only partly reset. Her brows remain tight, but she presses her phone to her ear after placing a live call to check whether Zuv is okay. She is not smiling and the scattered cushion residue remains visible.
slides.camera: Intimate side-medium single of Aachu, phone and tense expression clear, with the messy room carrying the unresolved argument.
slides.silent_read: Concern reaches him even while she is still angry.

slides.scene: Zuv has reached his own separate front door at night and answers the same call with his phone pressed to his ear while his other hand unlocks the door. He stands alone with his office bag and keys, expression softened only slightly, making the separate-home reality visible without wedding symbols or a staged ring close-up.
slides.camera: Quiet medium-wide exterior or landing shot with one person and one distinct home threshold.
slides.silent_read: They have separate official lives, but the emotional check-in already functions like partnership.

slides.scene: The next morning returns to the office-lobby or cafe geography from slide 1. Without discussion, Aachu brings Zuv's forgotten ID card while Zuv slides her already-ordered coffee toward her; they meet mid-step and exchange both things at once. The ordinary routine, not a wedding symbol, completes the story.
slides.camera: Wider match-cut to slide 1 with both reciprocal actions, relaxed recognition, and forward movement visible.
slides.silent_read: No vows have happened, but an automatic 'us' already has.

continuity_locks: Slides 1 and 11 form a deliberate morning habit match-cut; the later frame deepens rather than merely repeats the first.
Slides 4-9 keep the same evening wardrobe, living-room geography, problem material, sofa, cushions, and fight residue.
The problem is introduced as one person's burden on slide 4 and visibly becomes shared on slide 5.
The cushion fight on slide 6 is equal, energetic, and readable from body action; it is not a posed pillow-holding portrait.
Zuv moves only outward across slides 7-8. He never returns or reaches back into the home.
Slide 9 checks on him remotely from the same unresolved living room; it does not reunite them.
Slide 10 establishes his separate home before slide 11 restores their shared routine.
No random text, phone UI, wedding symbols, decorative hearts, extra narrative people, or generic romantic embrace.
